input.quote: Subject to the terms and conditions of this Agreement, MSL agrees to produce and sell, and IBM agrees to purchase Products. This Agreement does not authorize MSL to produce or deliver any Product.
input.rationale: No exclusivity, sole-source or requirements commitment is imposed on IBM anywhere in the Agreement, which meets the preferred position. Section 3.0 Scope of Work (p0102) simply describes MSL performing "selected manufacturing, Integration, and other Services", and Section 6.0 Purchase of Products (p0720) is purchase-order driven ("This Agreement does not authorize MSL to produce or deliver any Product") rather than a requirements contract; there is no "exclusive", "sole supplier", "all of its requirements" or "shall not procure from any third party" language (searches for "exclusive", "sole", "source", "requirements from", "other suppliers" return only unrelated uses, e.g. MSL's exclusive remedy and MSL buying parts "solely for use in IBM Products", which binds MSL, not us). Product Forecast (p0866) and Supply Flexibility (p0923) create supply-and-demand process and volume-flexibility obligations on MSL and expressly state IBM "will have no liability for unused flexibility", so IBM retains freedom to source elsewhere. The forecast-accuracy charges in Appendix 2 are a volume/forecast-liability point addressed under the applicable commitment rule, not an exclusivity restriction, so no redline is proposed here.
